### Project Name

anySQL

### Project Description

anySQL is an open-source Python library that records the telemetry of LLM applications, agents and RAG pipelines, and lets you query it with standard SQL. Transparent wrappers for the OpenAI and Anthropic clients, an agent tracer and a RAG tracer normalise telemetry into six canonical Apache Arrow tables: llm_responses, eval_results, pipeline_runs, agent_tool_calls, agent_trace and rag_chunks. The tables share join keys: session_id and a per-session step_order put model calls, retrievals and tool calls into one ordered sequence, and query_id links retrieved chunks to the evaluation of the answer they produced. Records are buffered in memory, optionally persisted to a single SQLite file, and queried in-process with DuckDB. There is no server, account or network call.

Why it's valuable. Cross-layer questions about agents, such as "did this RAG answer fail at retrieval or at generation?" or "was a value first seen in a tool output later passed to a state-changing tool call?", become a single SQL JOIN rather than a one-off parser over several log formats. Because the schema is fixed and documented, analyses are portable across experiments and can be versioned, hashed and published. Built-in analyses cover multi-model comparison, prompt regression detection, cost attribution, agent debugging (tool failure rates, loop detection, session diffs) and RAG failure-mode classification.

The repository also contains anysql-proxy, a local HTTP proxy between AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue, Zed) and the OpenAI/Anthropic APIs that logs tokens, cost, latency and editor context to DuckDB.

Origin and history. Started by Karthikeyan Sadayamuthu in March 2026 (v0.1.0 released 2026-03-10). v0.2.0 (November 2026) added the cross-layer step sequence, used as the measurement substrate of a peer-reviewed study of prompt-injection detection in agent telemetry (IEEE CSTA 2026, accepted). The current release is v0.3.1 (2026-11-19), on PyPI as anysql-sdk and archived on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23980548).

### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

The AAIF exists to give agentic AI open, neutrally governed infrastructure. As agents take actions on users' behalf, being able to inspect what an agent saw, decided and did, across model calls, retrievals and tool calls, is a precondition for trusting it. anySQL provides an open, embedded, vendor neutral way to do that: a documented relational schema for agent telemetry and plain SQL to query it, with no hosted service.

anySQL directly serves the topics of AAIF's Observability and Traceability working group (agent traces, tool-call provenance) and Security and Privacy working group (detecting prompt-injection compromises from recorded telemetry), and supports Accuracy and Reliability through regression detection and RAG failure analysis. The value of a shared telemetry schema grows with the number of tools that use it, which is best settled under neutral governance early.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

anySQL is complementary to existing AAIF projects and does not overlap with any of them. It is an analysis layer for the behaviour of agents built with them:

Model Context Protocol (MCP): MCP standardises how agents call tools; anySQL records and analyses those tool calls. MCP tool-call tracing (server and tool names into agent_tool_calls and the session step sequence) is on the roadmap.

goose and other agents: anySQL can record and query the sessions of agents like goose, and anysql-proxy already records the model calls of AI coding agents.

AGENTS.md: no direct relation; anySQL could be used to measure how agents behave with and without project instructions.

anySQL also plans import and export for the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, so it interoperates with telemetry collected by other tools rather than replacing them.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

**Use cases**

1. Agent debugging: tool failure rates, loop detection, session diffs and human intervention points over agent_tool_calls and agent_trace.
2. RAG forensics: joining rag_chunks to eval_results on query_id to classify failures as retrieval or generation.
3. Agent security: SQL detection rules over the step sequence, such as an identifier first seen in a tool output and later used in a state-changing call.
4. Model evaluation and cost: multi-model comparison, prompt regression detection and cost attribution by feature.
5. Studying AI coding assistants with anysql-proxy.

**Evidence**

anySQL is early stage and does not yet have documented production use outside the maintainer. 

Current evidence:
Measurement substrate of Untraced by Design: Hunting Prompt-Injection Compromises in LLM Agent Telemetry with SQL, IEEE CSTA 2026 (accepted). The study replays 11,652 recorded AgentDojo runs into anySQL through its public tracer API and evaluates six detection queries frozen by hash across four held-out models. Artefacts: https://github.com/sadayamuthu/untraced-by-design

- Software paper prepared for the Journal of Open Source Software (paper/).
- Released on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/anysql-sdk/
- Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23980548
- The Sandbox thesis explains why the project matters before adoption:
- https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/docs/aaif/THESIS.md

### Governance Model

anySQL uses a maintainer-based model adapted from Minimum Viable Governance,
documented in
[GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md).
Roles are users, contributors, maintainers and a lead maintainer. Decisions
are made by lazy consensus in issues and pull requests; schema-breaking
changes, major releases and governance changes need explicit majority
approval of maintainers, with the lead maintainer breaking ties. There is
currently one maintainer; GOVERNANCE.md sets out how contributors become
maintainers and states the goal of maintainers from at least two
organizations. On admission the project would adopt the LF technical charter.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

- **CI** (GitHub Actions, `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml`) runs on every
  pull request to `main`: pytest on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 (about 110 SDK
  tests, plus the proxy's own test suite), `ruff check` and
  `ruff format --check`, and a check that the version has been bumped.
- **Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) runs on merge to `main`: if
  the version in `pyproject.toml` is new, it builds a wheel and sdist, and
  publishes to PyPI from a protected `pypi` environment, then tags and
  creates a GitHub release.
- **Dependencies:** Dependabot opens weekly grouped updates for Python
  packages and GitHub Actions.
- **Release frequency:** five releases so far (v0.1.0 in March 2026; v0.1.1,
  v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 in November 2026). Releases are cut as features
  land, with semantic versioning; the project is pre-1.0.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

anySQL's specification is its six canonical table schemas, defined in
`anysql/schema.py` and documented in the README, with reference queries in
`docs/QUERIES.md`. Changes go through public GitHub issues and pull requests,
as described in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
larger changes start with an issue to agree the approach, every behaviour
change needs a test, and CI must pass. Under
[GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md),
removing, renaming or retyping a schema column needs explicit majority
approval of maintainers. A documented schema versioning and migration policy
is planned for 1.0 ([ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/ROADMAP.md)).

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

Leadership: Karthikeyan Sadayamuthu (lead maintainer).

Decisions are made by lazy consensus in public issues and pull requests (at
least 72 hours for anything beyond a small fix). Schema-breaking changes,
major releases, contested maintainer changes and governance changes need
explicit majority approval of maintainers; the lead maintainer breaks ties
and records the reason publicly. While there is one maintainer, that
maintainer decides and records the reason in the issue or pull request. See
[GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md).

### Security

No OpenSSF Best Practices badge yet. Current posture:

- Vulnerabilities are reported privately through GitHub security advisories;
  [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/sadayamuthu/anysql/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
  sets out a precise threat model and what is in and out of scope.
- anySQL runs in-process and makes no network calls of its own. Recorded
  values are written with parameterised SQLite statements, and the adapters
  do not record API keys, headers or client configuration.
- `anysql-proxy` stores provider API keys encrypted (Fernet) in
  `~/.anysql/keys.toml`.
- PyPI publishing runs from a protected GitHub environment, and GitHub
  Actions workflows use read-only default permissions.
- Dependabot keeps Python and Actions dependencies current.

### Additional Information

anySQL is pre-1.0 and early stage, and applies to Sandbox because a shared,
neutrally governed relational schema for agent telemetry is most useful if it
is settled before incompatible schemas proliferate. The project plans to
interoperate with OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions and MCP rather than
compete with them, and would welcome guidance from the Observability and
Traceability working group.

Note: the `docs.anysql.org` documentation site is not live yet;
a docs site is the first item on the roadmap.
